verified_key_information_units.information: Segment and geographic revenue distribution: Business divided into two segments - SAF products (CFIP, Integra, Spectrum Compact, Aranet) dominating revenue, and other products (antennas, cables, OEM); exports account for 97% of group turnover (EUR 25.24 million) and 96% of parent turnover (EUR 21.06 million), with products sold in 87 countries.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Vadības ziņojums (eksports), 17. piezīme (segmenti un ģeogrāfiskā sadalījuma informācija)

verified_key_information_units.information: Loss explanation and outlook: Management characterizes the reporting year's loss as temporary and not impacting long-term stability; focuses on strategic market niches for wireless data transmission products and specialized solutions.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Vadības ziņojums (zaudējumu situācijas vērtējums un nākotnes plāni)

candidate_sentences.text: Management considers the loss temporary but remains cautious because of tariff uncertainty, geopolitical conditions and continued dependence on international markets.

verified_key_information_units.information: Proposal to cover loss: Board of Directors proposes to cover the reporting year's loss from retained earnings of previous years.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, K4, K5, and K7 are PRESENT with supporting sentences identified. K6 is MISSING as there is no mention of segment breakdown (SAF products vs other products) or geographic revenue distribution details (export percentages or country count). K8 is MISSING as there is no mention of the board's proposal to cover the loss from retained earnings. The summary captures most core financial performance, regional changes, geopolitical impact, product development, and liquidity positions, but omits critical structural and governance elements, justifying a 'Generally yes' score.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is fully coherent internally. All statements are logically connected and support the overall narrative of improved financial performance despite ongoing losses. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational problems. The summary flows logically from revenue performance to profitability metrics, then to balance sheet changes and operational context. While there is a minor numerical relationship between segment revenues and the consolidated total (as is common in financial reporting), the candidate does not claim these are exhaustive additive components of the same total, so this does not constitute a contradiction under the specified evaluation criteria. The structure is clear and each section builds upon the previous one without repetition or confusion.
